decisions.reason: The tolerance interface is binary encoding of a rational, not a restriction to dyadic values: def-qa-37-certified-matrix-input explicitly records numerator/denominator encoding length and specializes def-qc-effective-unitary-matrix-input, which requests a positive rational in binary. Thus 1/3 is supplied by binary integers 1 and 11. The B6 procedure compares rational quantities exactly and never requires a power-of-two tolerance denominator. Its proof bounds coordinate error by 2*d*sqrt(2)*2^(-p)<3*d*2^(-p), uses joint density at epsilon/128 and the bound sqrt(2)*d^(3/2)<=32 for d<=8, then obtains a strict certificate at finite precision by convergence and dovetailing. AComega enters through density only; no search-time bound is inferred.

The input is a certified base-net certificate in the gate-package sense, not an arbitrary real-radius net. def-qa-37-fibonacci-braid-gate-set explicitly defines that certificate by def-qc-inverse-closed-dense-su2-gate-set, whose Definition says to fix a rational 0<eta0<1/4096 and coverage eta0/4. Both are listed algorithm dependencies, so the finite branch already inherits the rational-radius hypothesis of thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-bit-complexity. Its algebraic-coordinate descriptions, polynomial unary Cauchy name, fixed certificate and binary numerator/denominator tolerance meet the remaining input conditions. The ideal branch separately invokes the decreasing-level exact-real recursion. Expanded labels have the recorded exponent sum and physical scalar (R1/z)^k; no effective base-net construction or exact-real access from a Cauchy name is asserted.

A supplied base-net certificate for G_Fib inherits def-qa-37-fibonacci-braid-gate-set Definition, which explicitly uses the certificate of def-qc-inverse-closed-dense-su2-gate-set; that definition requires a rational radius and eta0/4 coverage. An irrational eta0 therefore is not an admitted certificate, and step 2.1 does satisfy the cited bit theorem. Independently, q_j=4096*eta_j obeys q_(j+1)=q_j^(3/2) with 0<q_0<1, so the least finite J exists, including J=0 at epsilon=eta0. The ideal resource supplier yields error <=epsilon and length <=L0*5^J, whose logarithmic exponent is log_(3/2)(5). The finite bound uses the stated algebraic isolation, fixed net, polynomial Cauchy-name and rational encoding hypotheses. The scalar (R1/z)^k follows from the exponent sum and is kept separate from normalized operator error; AComega is carried only for density.
